scope: The sim -> paper -> live gate ladder for the selected destination (NautilusTrader 2.0.0rc5 with IBKR primary and a separate Alpaca paper adapter; LEAN 985ef30 frozen oracle). Each gate names the receipt that establishes it and the machine-checkable condition that flips it. scripts/trading_gates.py --check verifies the ladder arithmetically; a status changes only by a dated commit after the checker lists the gate as a flip candidate; an exists condition proves only that a non-empty file is present, so gates using it carry a presence-only limitation in their note. Rung readiness = every required gate of that rung and every earlier rung established. Nothing here authorizes live configuration, paid hosting or orders.

rung_meaning.sim: historical simulation qualified on the destination engine against the frozen oracle and clean data
rung_meaning.paper: paper operation qualified: broker path exercised, alerts wired, credentials handled, snapshots gated
rung_meaning.live: live entry prerequisites: paper leverage ladder, native fault behaviour, IBKR acceptance, explicit go

live-go.note: Authorship control for the explicit live go, 2026-09-25. scripts/trading_gates.py counts live-go as holding only when docs/decisions/live-go.md is non-empty and `ssh-keygen -Y verify -f docs/decisions/live-go.allowed_signers -I live-go-signer -n live-go@native-agent-stack -s docs/decisions/live-go.md.sig` accepts its exact committed bytes. It fails closed: an absent or empty document, signature or allowed_signers file, a path that resolves outside the tree, no ssh-keygen, a timeout or a failed verification leaves live-go not holding, so it cannot count as established and stays in blocking.live (an established live-go that does not verify is also an error). Recorded established, live-go must carry evidence_class user_decision. Only the user creates the signing key, the allowed_signers entry, live-go.md and its signature; the one-time setup is in catalogs/us-equities/README.md, and automation never does any of it. None of the three files existed when this control was added. Limits: the allowed_signers file lives in the tree, so anyone with write access can replace it; a replacement shows in that file's diff and history but the checker does not prevent it, and a hardware-backed key that needs a physical touch keeps agent sessions from signing with the registered key. Design record: docs/decisions/2026-09-25-live-go-authorship-control.md.

gates.title: Adaptive paper runtime completes a regular-session broker trial
gates.note: Established 2026-09-23 on a main-built trial: blueprints/us-equities/adaptive-paper/receipt.json broker_readiness passed, trial adaptive-20260923g from a read-only git archive of main 843dc8f (all three #123 engine fixes). 300.5 s at 1x on SIP, 5 real paper orders with 1 cancel-replace and 4 native fills over two 1-share round trips (INTC, GOOGL), 134 crossed quotes dropped, reconciled flat with cash and positions matching, realized -0.28 USD; the read-only broker readback matches (trials/20260923g-main-passed/). Evidence of engine and broker order flow at 1x, not strategy edge. Precondition replaced (dated decision 2026-09-23): the earlier note required Codex's 1e2c96a interrupted-run reporting on main before a flip; that is replaced by direct checks on paper-output.json (elapsed 300.48 s of 300; 147 decision events spanning 299.04 s with a largest gap of 2.11 s; independent review of #128 reproduced both). Overturn: a main trial that includes f75a3d2's interrupted-run reporting and flags this build's behaviour as interrupted. History before this flip: Receipt then: status local_integration_passed_new_broker_trial_pending, broker_readiness not_started (regular_session_window_unavailable). Synthetic capacity fixture (180 fills / 90 round trips in 60.42 s) used zero broker connections and is not this gate. Authorized paper work, not run by the 2026-09-22 handbook wave. 2026-09-22 10:55 ET: one SIP trial in the default state root ended completed_no_signals in 0.35 s with 0 orders and a flat reconciliation, which does not meet the flip condition. Root cause measured: the Windows host clock was +0.64 s off NTP and WSL's hv_utils time sync pulled the guest to it, so live quotes looked future-stamped and tripped the transport's -0.25 s quote guard (quote_timestamp_stale -> start_not_ready); an environment fault, not an engine or feed fault. Next attempt needs `w32tm /resync /force` on the host (user OS action) and, since PR-4, a passing promotion-gate result for the paper command (--gate-result/--snapshot). Ownership passed to peer:sota-workflow-resolution with adaptive-paper integration on 2026-09-22. 2026-09-23 (engine outputs and labelled operator observations in blueprints/us-equities/adaptive-paper/trials/20260923-interrupted/): the scheduled 10:05 ET timer for frozen 41d39b3 was stopped externally at 09:39:24 ET (actor unidentified); relaunched at 10:11:05 ET from the same frozen archive. Ingest 480 rows and the promotion gate passed, but the runner stopped after 4.15 s of 300 (3 warm-up decisions, regime unavailable, 8,512 native quotes, 0 orders, flat) and reported completed_no_signals. The log shows a trading-stream websocket restart message; corrected at 11:30 ET: that message is emitted when the engine closes its own streams at shutdown, not the cause (the transport alone stayed healthy for 25 s). A clock-offset check about 13 minutes later found 0.06 s against NTP (operator observation), so the 2026-09-22 clock fault is unlikely. An interrupted decision loop is needs_attention, not a trial; no retry of 41d39b3. 2026-09-23 11:27 ET second attempt (blueprints/us-equities/adaptive-paper/trials/20260923b-needs-attention/): from Codex's frozen stop-diagnostics build 1e2c96a, needs_attention after 25.9 s. Recorded: decision_exit transport_gap, callback_failure at stage quote_normalization (normalize_quote raised TransportError). Most likely a crossed SIP quote (bid above ask), the only rejection class in the committed quote-validity measurements; for the 10:11 run it is only a possible explanation (the retained crossed-quote rates vary widely by minute, from 0 to 36 per 60 s window, so the chance of one among its 8,512 quotes ranges from about 15 percent to near certainty; that build recorded no stop reason). 11:42 and 11:5x ET runs from integration build 796e3d1 (1e2c96a plus the crossed-quote fix; trials/20260923c-reconcile-refusal/) reached the 30 s reconciliation and failed there: transport.mark_reconciled refused while any event was queued, and on SIP the quote queue is never empty (traceback retained). Fixed by dropping and counting well-formed crossed or one-sided quotes (halt-flagged, malformed or unsubscribed ones still fail closed) and refusing reconciliation only while an order event is queued. Gate unchanged until a trial completes. 11:54 ET run from integration build 885663a (both SIP fixes; trials/20260923e-first-roundtrip/): the first real engine round trip on the paper broker, INTC buy 1 filled 120.40 then recovery sell 1 filled 120.39, flat, net -0.01 USD; it stopped at 43.3 s with adapter_error because the fill TradeId (UUID + ':cum:' + qty, 42 characters) exceeds Nautilus's 36-character limit. Fixed with a deterministic 36-character digest. 11:59 ET: first PASSED 1x trial (trials/20260923f-first-passed/) from integration build 5e1d512 (1e2c96a plus all three #123 fixes): 300.1 s, duration_completed, 8 real paper orders and 8 native fills over four 1-share round trips (GOOGL, AAPL, AMZN, INTC), 13 crossed quotes dropped, reconciled flat with cash and positions matching, realized -0.29 USD; the broker readback matches. The gate stays not_established until 1e2c96a's commits and #123 are on main and a main-built trial passes, so the flip receipt binds to published code. Regular session only (2026-09-23, status unchanged): extended hours are not qualified. The first extended-hours paper run (trials/20260923-post-extended-hours, 19:01 ET, the same risk limits except max_held_symbols 4 for a 4-symbol universe) stopped after 10.9 s with 0 orders, flat and reconciled; a data-timeout reconnect was logged but the stop reason is not recorded. The 3 s quote-age cap and the benchmark-freshness preflight are in code, and a retained 19:20 ET SIP sample had all four benchmarks fresh at once in 3 of 8 snapshots; the remedy is an open design question for a limits decision.

gates.title: Broker credential handling decided and enforced in code (0600 env file, owner uid, outside any worktree)
gates.note: Decision recorded and enforced in runner.credentials() (0600, owner uid, outside any worktree) with unit tests (unit pr4-gate-credentials). 2026-09-24: the market_research.py gap is closed -- both loaders now call the shared credential_guard.open_verified(), so the rules cannot drift between them; runner.credentials() keeps resolving a symlink to its target (follow_symlinks=True) while market_research.credentials() keeps refusing a symlink outright (follow_symlinks=False, its prior O_NOFOLLOW behavior), and runner's asserted error-string prefix is unchanged. 2026-09-24 fix round 2 (independent Codex security review, 'not ready'): from '/', every ancestor directory opens as O_DIRECTORY|O_NOFOLLOW via dir_fd chaining (never a resolved-pathname re-open) and the final component opens O_RDONLY|O_NOFOLLOW|O_NONBLOCK|O_NOCTTY the same way, so a symlink substituted at any position fails closed with ELOOP/ENOTDIR; the final file must have exactly one hard link. 2026-09-24 fix round 3 (same Codex review returned 'not ready' again, plus an independent Claude real-mutation/attack run: 260 attack cases and a live RENAME_EXCHANGE race, all refused): every ancestor from '/' down through the immediate parent -- not only the immediate parent -- must be owned by root or the caller, and group/other-writable only if sticky (OpenSSH safe_path/secure_filename), closing a rename-an-already-checked-ancestor attack where only the immediate parent was checked; a symlink-loop RuntimeError (Python 3.12's Path.resolve(strict=True), not OSError) and an embedded-NUL ValueError are now caught, and every raised error is built outside the except block that caught the original failure so __context__ cannot carry it either; a '..' path component is refused outright for market_research's non-follow mode instead of lexically collapsed (which could skip an intermediate symlink); the verified descriptor is closed if fdopen() itself fails; GUARD_DENIED's single message is replaced with a small set of fixed credential_file_permissions:<code> reason codes (owner, mode, hardlink, worktree, ancestor, parent_owner, parent_mode, symlink, not_regular, missing, encoding, size); runner.credentials()'s read is now bounded the same way market_research's is (cap+1 bytes from the fd, not the whole file or an earlier fstat size). This is NOT a guarantee against a worktree configured purely through GIT_DIR/GIT_WORK_TREE or core.worktree with no .git entry in the file's own ancestor chain, nor against a bind-mounted repository subdirectory outside all visible .git ancestors in this process's own mount namespace (both undetectable by a file-local check), nor against a same-shaped replacement file an equally-privileged actor swaps in at the exact instant of the real open() (the fd read is whatever passed its own checks at that instant, by construction, not a TOCTOU gap -- runner's symlink-follow mode documents this same acceptance for a symlink whose target changes before the traversal). Covered by tests.test_adaptive_paper_runner.CredentialFilePermissions (existing, still passing, plus symlink/FIFO/hardlink/non-ASCII cases, FIFO cases now signal.alarm-deadline-bounded), tests.test_adaptive_paper_runner.SharedCredentialGuardParity, tests.test_adaptive_market_research.MarketResearchCredentialFilePermissions (wrong mode, wrong owner, symlink, inside a Git worktree, missing file, a deadline-bounded FIFO, hard link, a valid file), and tests/test_adaptive_paper_credential_race.py (the real filename -- an earlier note named a nonexistent tests/test_credential_guard_race.py): its HookInjectedRaces/AncestorRenameResistance/NoPathLeakInErrors/DotDotIsRejected/FdOpenFailureCleanup/FdLeakOnRefusal/RootMarkerIsChecked/ForeignFileOwnerAloneIsRejected/FstatNotPathnameStat/BoundedReadIsActuallyBounded classes exercise the round-3 findings (hook-injected mid-walk worktree marker; simulated foreign ownership via per-fd fstat faking, not a process-wide os.getuid() patch that would also fail the parent check and mask the result; __context__/__cause__ assertions; real /proc fd-count checks around success and every refusal; and the exact read() size argument each loader uses, not only the outcome, since a static oversized fixture rejects identically either way). Its RealMutationKills class replaces an earlier in-process MUTATION_KILLS meta-test (which asserted a hardcoded string-to-test-name mapping without ever running those tests, per the round-2 Codex review) with a driver (tests/_credential_mutation_driver.py) that copies the real source tree to a private temporary directory, applies one real exact-count textual mutation, and runs the actually-named test(s) against that copy in a subprocess; all twelve currently-declared mutations are killed this way. 2026-09-24 fix round 4 (both reviewers again found no access-rule bypass: 268 attack cases and a live rename-exchange race, about 600k swaps; 31 of 33 real mutations already killed): both loaders now check raw.isascii() on the bytes before ever decoding, so no UnicodeDecodeError (whose .object attribute holds the entire file, secret included) is ever constructed, closing a path where __context__ carried the whole credential file even though the message itself was clean; the mutation driver was corrected -- it counted any non-zero subprocess exit as a kill, so disable_worktree_check reported KILLED on completely unmutated code because the copy had no .git; it now git-inits every copy, runs the named tests on the pristine copy first (must pass), and counts a kill only on a genuine FAIL (never an ERROR, never a bare non-zero exit) -- all fourteen mutations (the original twelve plus two new ones below) are killed under the corrected rule, and MutationDriverSelfTests proves the driver itself does not report a false kill; the final os.fdopen(file_fd, 'rb') call was replaced with io.FileIO(file_fd, 'rb', closefd=True) built first and only that object (never the bare fd) closed if wrapping it later fails, avoiding a double-close/EBADF if FileIO's own constructor is what fails; two more mutations were added and killed (skipping root's own ownership/mode check; removing runner's size check, which previously silently truncated an oversized file at the cap and could pass its early lines through as an apparently-valid, truncated credential); the immediate parent is tightened back from round 3's relaxation -- owned by exactly the caller, never root, and never group/other-writable, with no sticky exception, so a bare /tmp/file or /file no longer loads, while a private directory under /tmp still does; a symlinked *directory* component (as opposed to the final file) is now reported as :symlink, not the generic :missing, via one extra failure-path-only lstat (Linux reports ENOTDIR, not ELOOP, for O_DIRECTORY|O_NOFOLLOW against a symlink); market_research's oversized-file rejection now raises the same credential_file_permissions:size code runner uses, closing the last reason-code inconsistency; and the decision doc no longer claims an atomic location guarantee for the worktree marker check -- it is a snapshot at each ancestor's own inspection time, and another uid permitted to write into a sticky ancestor (e.g. /tmp) can still create a new .git entry there afterward. 2026-09-24 fix round 5 (both reviewers again found no access-rule bypass: 288 attack cases and a live rename-exchange race, about 670k swaps; all 33 earlier mutations plus round 4's 14 killed, driver produced no false kills in 21 scenarios) -- the final small items: _is_symlink_component()'s failure-path lstat caught only OSError, so a NUL byte or a surrogate in an ancestor directory component escaped as a bare ValueError/UnicodeEncodeError instead of the sanitized code, now caught alongside OSError; the io.FileIO double-close fix's own comment was wrong (io.FileIO(fd, closefd=True) does NOT close fd itself on a failed construction, verified against CPython, so that specific failure was actually leaking the fd, not risking a double-close) and is now closed with a plain os.close(file_fd) only in that one case, with only the already-constructed raw object (never the bare fd) closed afterward; added tests that fail when the stricter immediate-parent rule (round 4) or the double-close fix is reverted, which previously passed the suite either way, plus a direct test that a symlinked directory component reports :symlink not :missing; and the mutation driver's skipped result, which fell through to survived, is now reported as inconclusive and fails the gate the same as a genuine survival. openbao stays conditional. Presence-only condition: the checker verifies that a non-empty file exists at receipt_path, not its content; qualification of what the file establishes is manual and the status changes only by a dated commit.

gates.title: Paper leverage ladder rung 1x completes with zero needs_attention and achieved gross leverage above 0.5x
gates.note: Leverage policy leverage-schedule-v1-20260922 implemented (SYN, opt-in; receipt block leverage_schedule_v1 in blueprints/us-equities/adaptive-paper/receipt.json; rung config config-leverage-1x.json); receipts record achieved peak leverage and time above the next-lower rung, and a rung establishes the envelope at its cap. Required rung receipt schema, preregistered 2026-09-24 (audit gap #5; no ladder receipt exists yet): {"schema_version": 1, "kind": "leverage_ladder_rung_receipt", "rung": "1x", "needs_attention": <int count of runs that ended needs_attention>, "source": {"paper_output_path": <repository-relative path of the certified run's committed paper-output.json>, "paper_output_sha256": <that file's sha256>, "certified_run_status": <that file's top-level "status">}, "leverage": <that file's "leverage" block (runner.run_native's outcome), copied verbatim>}. flip_condition is an all_of: /schema_version == 1, /kind == "leverage_ladder_rung_receipt", /rung == "1x", /needs_attention == 0, /source/certified_run_status == "passed", a source_matches binding (scripts/trading_gates.py: the file at /source/paper_output_path must exist in the tree and hash to /source/paper_output_sha256, and its /leverage and /status must equal the receipt's /leverage and /source/certified_run_status exactly, so the leverage block and the certified run's passed status come from the one hashed run), /leverage/config_max_leverage == "1", /leverage/next_lower_rung_ceiling == "0.5" (leverage.next_lower_rung_ceiling for this rung -- the documented 0.5x minimum exposure, since 1x has no lower rung), /leverage/peak_achieved_leverage > 0.5 and /leverage/seconds_above_next_lower_rung_ceiling > 0 (scripts/trading_gates.py greater_than accepts the runner's decimal strings and JSON numbers). A trial that never exceeds 0.5x gross-to-equity leverage therefore cannot flip this gate (tests/test_trading_gates.py LeverageLadderFlipConditionTests). Limits: needs_attention counts every run at this rung and is not bound to the hashed file, so it is checked against the rung's trial directories at the manual qualification; seconds_above is a per-tick approximation (runner._leverage_achievement_step attributes the whole tick gap), and no minimum duration above 0.5x is set -- any positive time satisfies the condition, so how long the rung was used is read from the receipt and judged at the manual qualification before the dated flip commit. First paper attempt 2026-09-24 (trial ladder-1x-20260924a, blueprints/us-equities/adaptive-paper/trials/ladder-1x-20260924a-needs-attention/): needs_attention after 190 s of 300 on a false-positive fill-precision refusal (order_cumulative_fill_precision_requires_reconciliation, the defect class of PR #205; the broker's fill activities show on-grid executions), flat and reconciled, peak achieved leverage 0.151 with 0 s above 0.5x; a retained failed attempt, not a flip receipt. leverage-schedule-v1-20260922 (agent-lab docs/decisions/2026-09-22-leverage-schedule-and-entitlement.md): 1x -> 2x -> 4x, each with its own receipt and zero needs_attention before the next rung; paper stays at 200 requests/minute.
